answer: Social-graph distance weighting stops a sybil cluster from inflating itself. Attestations are weighted by distance on a public mirror of the trust graph: inside one cluster they count near zero, while a bridge attestation from another community counts in full. A cluster with no outside links sits like a lagoon, endorsing itself in a pool that earns no weight. Running 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 bridge links at 10 joint tasks each, so cost grows per fake. Cluster farming fails: a fresh cluster starts at zero weight, while one bridge link gives an honest agent full weight.
